basis: Token counts returned per request (5.55M input tokens) at TypeSafe's $42 per billion input tokens
name: Jev reads
result: It tells the original documents from the rewrites every time and finds leftover unnamed jobs, but mostly not sentences that still take dentistry or a job for granted: in set 7 it flagged none of the 3 documents that still point to dentistry, in set 8 one of 3, and in set 9, after the whole-document review, not the one left (a sponsor's “working athlete” clause).
title: Jev (TypeSafe's reader model, jev-1.13.0) read 800 documents paragraph by paragraph and whole: the original texts of set 6 and seven rounds of rewrites (sets 4 to 9). For each passage it gives the probability that a reader would suspect he is a dentist, works in health care, or has a job.
why: Gabriel: check the rewrites with Jev instead of a Claude check pass, and read only what Jev suspects.
